source_control_note: Original ECF 1320-39 was struck on 2024-01-04 for personally identifiable information. GAH does not republish that copy and cites the redacted refiling ECF 1326-4 for Log 153. Update 2026-10-06: ECF 264-1 confirms Judge Sweet reviewed the law-enforcement materials in camera, upheld the qualified public-interest privilege, denied compelled disclosure, and ordered the log and documents preserved under seal. Update 2026-10-06: the 2019 BSF subpoena and released March/April production indexes were mapped. The subpoena expressly excluded validly privileged documents; the reviewed indexes do not identify a separate approximately 57-document law-enforcement tranche. DOJ direct automated PDF retrieval was age-gated during this pass, so no local hash is asserted for the added EFTA sources.

limits: Privilege logs are metadata, not the withheld contents.
Party briefing is adversarial advocacy unless separately adopted by a court.
The phrase 'Defendant and others' does not identify the others.
Names in the record do not imply wrongdoing.
The 2016 privilege ruling establishes judicial review and protection of the submitted materials; it does not identify the agency, unnamed others, contents, investigative theory, or disposition.
The August 2026 protective-order modification does not by itself prove the approximately 57 documents were among the 2019 subpoenaed BSF materials or were released under EFTA.

The released BSF production indexes do not prove that Log 153 materials were absent from every DOJ channel; they establish only that no matching approximately 57-document tranche is identified in the reviewed indexes.
